messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The test `testLang412Left()` tries to append a null value with a fixed width left pad using method `appendFixedWidthPadLeft(null, 10, '*');`. The bug report indicates that this operation causes a NullPointerException if the `nullText` property has not been set.

From the code snippet of `StrBuilder.appendFixedWidthPadLeft(Object obj, int width, char padChar)`, the method handles the padding by first converting the object `obj` to a string `str`. This is done by checking if `obj` is null; if so, it assigns `str` to the value of `getNullText()`, otherwise it uses `obj.toString()`.

The method `getNullText()` simply returns the internal field `nullText`, which can be null if not explicitly set.

The NullPointerException occurs because if `obj` is null and `nullText` has not been explicitly set, `getNullText()` will return null. Then later in the method, the code calls `str.length()` and `str.getChars(...)`. Since `str` is null, any of these calls cause a NullPointerException.

Therefore, the root cause is that `appendFixedWidthPadLeft` does not safely handle the case where `obj` is null and `nullText` is not set. It assumes `getNullText()` returns a non-null string, which is not guaranteed by the existing code.

In essence, a missing null check on the result of `getNullText()` before calling string methods is causing the NPE.

This diagnosis matches the bug report and the test failure perfectly.

Next, I can identify the best methods to fix this.
org.apache.commons.lang.text.StrBuilder.appendFixedWidthPadLeft(java.lang.Object, int, char)

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
